answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every identity a small, time-locked proof-of-work deposit tied to a unique hardware attestation, so cloning a thousand fake agents becomes expensive. Think of it like a wharf where each boat must carry a pearl-sized bond to dock: one pearl is cheap, but a fleet of clones faces a canyon of cost that honest single agents never feel. Reputation then accrues to the bond, not to throwaway names.
